title: The new sets fall, the old cards rise
headline: The new sets fall and the old cards rise. We can't say why.
dek: Since Oct 13 the board's 7-day list has published 330 rows. 128 came from the Mega Evolution sets, and 121 of them were down. The other 202 came from every older set, and 172 were up. Since Nov 3 it is starker: 88 Mega Evolution rows, all down; 32 older-set rows, 27 up. The risers aren't one card: 85 different older cards have made the list on the way up, from Lugia EX (Team Plasma) to Giratina at $451.70 and Snorlax at $286.31. Every one is unconfirmed.
why_now: Thursday's and Saturday's Files were about cards from one set falling. Zoom out and the pattern runs across sets: it is the cleanest thing the 7-day list has shown in six weeks, and also the easiest to over-read, so it is the week to say how much of it we can and can't stand behind.
risk: The list is not the market. It shows cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more and trade often, so which cards qualify depends partly on which sets are new. A newer set may be showing its early prices settling, and an older card needs only a few sales to move; the price data shows the movement, not which of these is happening, and not why. 85 different older cards is a spread, but each rise is one week on a thin market, and 7 Mega Evolution rows did go up. No sale was checked behind any of it. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether a Mega Evolution card makes the 7-day list on the way up for more than a day or two: since Oct 13, 7 of its 128 rows have. Whether the older cards' rises hold, such as Giratina (Team Plasma) at $451.70 and Snorlax at $286.31, both last read on Nov 11. And the label: the morning one of these cards has a checked sale, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's published 7-day lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026 (33 mornings; readings Oct 12 to Nov 13)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The counts: the board's own published 7-day lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026, 33 mornings (git history of data/movers.json), 10 rows a morning, 330 in all (Oct 13 is when the 3-day-median rule began). "Mega Evolution" here means a set whose name begins ME (ME: Mega Evolution Promo, ME: 30th Celebration, ME06: Delta Reign, and so on): 128 rows, 121 down, 7 up. "Older" means every other set: 202 rows, 172 up, 30 down. Since Nov 3: 120 rows, 88 Mega Evolution (88 down) and 32 older (27 up). 85 different older cards had at least one rising row. A card counts once per morning it was listed. The table: four cards from the Nov 14 list (readings through Nov 13); start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades (its price changed on 3 or more of the last 14 days). Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
